issues.t: Balance shaft gear wear (check engine light, P0016/P0017)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often on the highway, with camshaft/crankshaft timing codes P0016 or P0017. Left alone it can turn into a timing chain rattle, rough running or engine failure.
issues.why: Early versions of the 3.5L V6 used a balance shaft gear that was not hard enough. The timing chain wears its teeth down, the chain goes slack and the valve timing drifts.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the timing checked soon. Ask a Mercedes specialist to confirm the gear wear before agreeing to a quote, because the repair is labor-heavy; some owners compare it with fitting a used later engine.

issues.t: 7-speed automatic harsh shifts or limp mode (valve body)
issues.sym: Hard or banging shifts, especially 2nd to 1st when slowing down, getting stuck in one gear, or the car going into limp mode where it will barely accelerate. A warning light may come on.
issues.why: The 7-speed automatic's valve body and its electronic conductor plate (with speed sensors) wear or fail. Worn solenoid magnets and old fluid make it worse.
issues.next: Get the transmission scanned for stored codes. A software update or fluid service can help mild cases, but limp mode usually needs a valve body or conductor plate replacement.

issues.t: Air suspension (Airmatic) sagging or "too low" warning
issues.sym: One corner or the whole car sits low after parking, the ride gets harsh, or the dash shows a "vehicle too low" warning telling you to stop.
issues.why: The rubber air springs dry out and crack with age and leak air. On cars with the self-leveling rear, the rear springs fail most often.
issues.next: Don't drive far with the too-low warning, since the compressor can burn out trying to keep up. Have the leaking air spring found and replaced; both sides of an axle are often done together.

issues.t: Air suspension compressor failure
issues.sym: The car won't rise after starting, a suspension warning appears, or you hear the compressor running for a long time.
issues.why: The compressor wears out, often because a leaking air spring made it run too much.
issues.next: Fix any air leak at the same time as the compressor, or the new one will fail early.

issues.t: Camshaft adjuster solenoid failure or oil leak
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with rough idle or poor pickup, and oil seeping at the front of the engine around the round camshaft magnets.
issues.why: The solenoids (magnets) that control variable valve timing fail, and oil can wick through them into the wiring.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing the solenoids is a modest job, but check the wiring connectors for oil too; oil in the harness can damage the engine computer.

issues.t: Intake manifold cracking or runner flap failure
issues.sym: Rough idle, loss of power, poorer fuel economy and a check engine light. In bad cases the engine stalls and shakes.
issues.why: The plastic intake manifold and its internal flaps get brittle and clogged with oily carbon from the crankcase vent system, and parts break.
issues.next: A shop can confirm with codes and a visual check. The usual fix is a new intake manifold.

issues.t: Power steering pump noise or leaks
issues.sym: Whining or groaning when turning, power steering fluid on the ground or around the pump, and heavy steering. Rarely the steering can go heavy suddenly at low speed.
issues.why: The power steering pump, its reservoir and hoses wear and leak with age.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. Replace a noisy or leaking pump before it fails, and never drive with the reservoir empty.

issues.t: Power steering rack leaking
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips under the front of the car, the fluid level keeps dropping, and steering may feel heavier or notchy.
issues.why: Seals in the steering rack (or its control valve) wear out and leak.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Small leaks can be monitored, but a leaking rack is eventually replaced with a new or rebuilt unit, followed by an alignment.

issues.t: Front differential failure (4MATIC)
issues.sym: Grinding, whining or clunking from the front of the car, especially when accelerating or turning, before the front differential fails.
issues.why: The front differential on the all-wheel-drive system wears out; several owners reported failures at 50,000 to 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the noise diagnosed early and check the differential oil. A failed unit is usually replaced.

issues.t: Front axle shaft (CV joint) wear
issues.sym: Clicking when turning, vibration, or grease thrown around the inside of the front wheel.
issues.why: The front drive axles of the 4MATIC system wear, and torn boots let grease out and dirt in.
issues.next: Inspect the front axle boots. Replace a leaking or clicking axle before the joint fails.

issues.t: Stuck in Park or shifter faults
issues.sym: The column shifter won't come out of Park, the shifter feels loose, or the transmission drops into limp mode with warnings, sometimes when the car is hot.
issues.why: The electronic shift module on the steering column or the transmission control unit fails.
issues.next: Have the transmission electronics scanned. The faulty shift module or control unit is usually replaced and programmed to the car.

issues.t: Rear lights failing or "substitute lights" message
issues.sym: Tail, brake or turn lights flicker or stop working, and the dash says a substitute light is on. New bulbs don't fix it.
issues.why: Worn bulb contacts, wiring in the tailgate area or the rear light module fail.
issues.next: Keep checking that your brake lights work. Ask the shop to check the wiring and connectors before replacing a control module.

issues.t: Heated seat overheating or burning
issues.sym: A burning smell from a seat, scorch marks on the cushion, and in one report a minor burn to the driver.
issues.why: The seat heating element can overheat.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater if you smell burning and have the seat inspected. A damaged heating element or seat cover must be replaced.

issues.t: Stalling from fuel pump or its wiring burning
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving and won't restart.
issues.why: Wiring between the engine harness and the fuel pump can overheat and burn, cutting power to the pump. A worn fuel pump causes similar stalling.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have the car towed in and the fuel pump circuit tested. Damaged wiring should be repaired along with the pump if needed.

issues.t: Power liftgate or tailgate latch failure
issues.sym: The rear hatch won't open or close with the button, or the latch won't release.
issues.why: The liftgate latch and its lock actuator wear out.
issues.next: Check the fuse first, then have the latch and actuator tested. Replacement fixes it.

issues.t: Door lock actuator failure
issues.sym: A door won't lock or unlock with the remote, or a rear door latch sticks and won't open.
issues.why: The lock actuator inside the door wears out.
issues.next: Have the door panel removed and the lock assembly replaced.

issues.t: Dead main or auxiliary battery and electrical faults
issues.sym: Slow cranking, warning messages, or random electrical glitches. Some owners also needed the fuse/relay (SAM) modules replaced.
issues.why: The R-Class has a main and an auxiliary battery; both wear out, and weak voltage triggers faults in the many control modules.
issues.next: Test both batteries before replacing modules. Replace weak batteries with the correct type.

issues.t: Thermostat failure (no heat or slow warm-up)
issues.sym: Little or no cabin heat, the temperature gauge reads low, or a check engine light for engine temperature.
issues.why: The thermostat sticks open with age.
issues.next: Have the cooling system checked; replacing the thermostat is a routine repair.

issues.t: ABS and stability warning from wheel speed sensor
issues.sym: ABS, ESP or brake warning lights come on, sometimes with cruise control cutting out.
issues.why: A wheel speed sensor fails, so the ABS and stability system switch off. Less often the ABS control module itself fails.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but have the code read. A single failed sensor is a common fix.

issues.t: Creaking front suspension (ball joints)
issues.sym: A creaking or groaning noise from the front over bumps or when turning at low speed.
issues.why: The front ball joints wear; an updated part is available.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected and worn joints or control arms replaced, then get an alignment.

issues.t: Oil seeping from back of cylinder heads
issues.sym: An oil smell or oil wetness at the back of the engine near the firewall.
issues.why: Small plugs at the back of the cylinder heads (cam plugs) and nearby seals leak with age.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the plugs resealed before oil drips onto hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Oil pan gasket leak
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine and the oil level drops between changes.
issues.why: The oil pan seal ages and leaks. On all-wheel-drive models the job is bigger because parts of the front drivetrain must come off.
issues.next: Keep the oil topped up and have the leak confirmed before paying for the larger repair.

issues.t: Turbodiesel turbocharger oil leak or failure
issues.sym: Blue smoke, oil around the turbo, loss of power and limp mode.
issues.why: The turbocharger's oil seal cracks or the turbo wears out on the 3.0L diesel.
issues.next: Stop driving hard and have the turbo inspected. Fixing it early can prevent oil from damaging other parts.

issues.t: Transmission oil cooler line leak (diesel)
issues.sym: Red or brown fluid drips at the front of the car and the transmission may shift poorly if the fluid gets low.
issues.why: The transmission cooler lines on diesel models leak at their crimped joints.
issues.next: Have the lines replaced and the transmission fluid level checked and topped up.

issues.t: A/C blowing warm (compressor or leak)
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only cools some of the time.
issues.why: Refrigerant leaks from lines, the condenser or evaporator, or the compressor or its pulley fails.
issues.next: Have a leak test done rather than just recharging. The fix depends on which part is leaking.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensors or exhaust manifold
issues.sym: Check engine light, possibly with a ticking exhaust sound or poorer fuel economy.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors fail, and on some cars the exhaust manifold cracks.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing oxygen sensors is common; a cracked manifold is a bigger job.
